name: Session cookies and tokens
plain: The cookie or token that keeps a person signed in between pages.
meaning: A random session ID (OWASP: at least 64 bits of entropy) ties each request to an account. Whoever holds it is the person. Timeouts are 2 to 5 minutes idle for high risk apps and up to 30 minutes for low risk, per OWASP.

web.api: Set-Cookie: sid=...; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; __Host- prefix

access.persistence: Session until browser close, or persistent up to 400 days. Idle and absolute server timeouts apply
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can keep you signed in between pages with a small ID stored in your browser
limits.user_action: Nothing extra. It starts when you sign in and continues as you click around
can: Remember who you are on every page you open until you sign out or it times out
Keep items in your cart or settings tied to your signed in session
Sign you out automatically after a set time, often 2 to 30 minutes of no activity
Treat anyone who holds that ID as you
cannot: Know who you are after the session ends or you clear cookies
Follow you onto other sites; the ID belongs to this site
Show your password; only a random session ID is stored
Stay valid after you sign out on a well built site

story.what_it_is: A small token that keeps you signed in as you move from page to page.
story.for_you: You sign in once and stay signed in while you click around, add things to a cart or play a web game. You never see the token. If it times out you are asked to sign in again.
story.for_makers: Every logged in site needs a way to remember who you are between clicks. Makers also use the same token to count active users, limit abuse, and tie purchases and saved progress to the right account.

use_cases.example: A browser game keeps a player signed in so a multiplayer match, friends list and in game purchases all point to the same account.
A cart stays full while a shopper browses for an hour, and the checkout page knows who they are.
A bank signs a person out after a few minutes of quiet and ties each session to one browser to block hijacking.
A video call web app keeps the host signed in while a meeting runs, so screen sharing and chat stay linked to their account.
A fraud engine watches for a session token suddenly used from a different country or device, which hints at theft.
A product team counts how many signed in people are active each day by counting session tokens.
A design web app keeps every browser tab signed in so edits sync live to a teammate's view.

technical_bounds: __Host- prefix forces Secure, Path=/ and no Domain
Browser restore can bring session cookies back after restart
